To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) the twist-2 parton model is not sufficient to describe the space-time structure of hadrons and the structure of hadrons in the transverse space is important;

the higher twist corrections to the structure functions of hadron are given by the time-ordered perturbation theory of the QCD improved parton model, and that the collinear singularity is naturally eliminated.

(1) a consistent and intuitive description can be achieved in a QCD improved parton model using the time-ordered perturbation theory where the collinear singularity is naturally eliminated; (2) the twist-4 contributions to the structure functions can be expressed in terms of the time-ordered Feynman diagrams with special propagators which are identified with backward propagators of the partons in time-ordering; (3) the time-ordered parton distribution functions are related to the conventional ones
In summary, our research is concerned with
the space-time properties of twist-4 corrections.
the development of a new generation of space-time integrators, based on a new class of numerical schemes, the so-called space-time adaptive integrators.
the study of the space-time properties of twist-four amplitudes in QCD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the twist-4 amplitudes are not just a mathematical artifact but a physical reality.

the twist-4 contributions to the hadron wave functions in QCD-improved perturbation theory are not only calculable, but can also be described in a consistent and intuitive manner, where the collinearity of the partons is naturally eliminated.

the space-time properties of the partonic structure functions are determined by the space-like and time-like propagators, and the space-time properties and dynamics of the partonic substructure are governed by the backward propagators.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are trying to find the space-time picture for the higher-twist amplitudes in the parton model.
we have developed a new approach to the higher twist corrections in the parton model and the QCD-improved version of the approach.
the higher twist corrections to the hadronic structure functions can be consistently and intuitively described in a QCD parton model, using time-ordered theory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the higher twist am- plitudes have a natural space-time description.
we have shown that the higher twist contributions to the hadron distribution functions are not only calculable but also consistent with the parton picture of the hadron.

the time-ordered perturbation theory provides a natural way of eliminating collinear singularities and thus of constructing a consistent and intuitive description for the higher twist corrections to the hadronic structure functions.
